A SEPARATE pnpm package, not a member of web/'s workspace. That workspace's
pnpm-workspace.yaml lists exactly one package ('app') and owns exactly one lockfile,
and FRONTEND-BFF.md §7 is emphatic that it stays that way. This package therefore
carries its own lockfile, which is what .github/workflows/ci.yml's e2e job checks for
by name before it will run. The package manager is still pnpm: one package manager for
the repository, two install roots.
WHY THERE IS NO POSTINSTALL BROWSER DOWNLOAD. `onlyBuiltDependencies: []` below tells
pnpm 10 to run no dependency lifecycle script, which includes playwright's browser
download. Browsers are installed by an explicit, greppable command instead — the same
one CI runs: `pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium`. An install that
silently pulls ~150 MB of browser binaries is an install nobody can audit, and it is
the reason a lockfile refresh in an unrelated PR sometimes takes four minutes.
EVERY SCRIPT HERE IS EXECUTED BY A CI CONTEXT. TESTING-STRATEGY.md §9: an unreferenced
test entry point is not a latent capability, it is documentation that lies. `test:smoke`
runs on pull_request and `test:full` on push to main, both in ci.yml's e2e job; the
remaining scripts are developer ergonomics over the same two projects, not a third
layer. There is deliberately no `test:extended` — see README.md.
`test:identity` is the third CI-executed entry point and it runs on BOTH events, which
is what issue #29 asks for. It is a SEPARATE script rather than `--project=identity`
appended to the other two, because the identity project exists only when the suite is
driving servers it started itself: against a deployed E2E_BASE_URL the project is
absent by design and `--project=identity` would fail with 'project not found' on a run
that is otherwise correct. See playwright.config.ts.
